# Story 01 — Tasks and reminders

## Prerequisites

- Story 20 (unified agent dashboard, agent-workspace) — the personal to-do list surfaces on that dashboard. If not yet complete, expose the reminder list as a self-contained section on `frontend/app/dashboard/page.tsx` and coordinate placement when Story 20 lands.
- Story 21 (agent availability toggle) already established the `me` self-scoped route pattern used here (see `backend/src/routes/me.routes.ts` lines 35–67).
- Story 54 (ticket-management, in-app notifications) already established the `Notification` model and `createTicketNotification` service (see `backend/src/models/Notification.ts`, `backend/src/services/notification.service.ts`). This story **extends** both rather than inventing parallel infrastructure.
- Story 27 (sla-automation, breach alerts) also needs a proactive scheduler. If Story 27 has landed by the time this is executed, **reuse the scheduler pattern** it introduced (grep for `setInterval` in `backend/src/services/`) instead of adding a second one. If not, this story introduces the first scheduler and Story 27 must reuse this one.

---

## Story Goal

An authenticated agent (or admin) can attach a personal reminder to any ticket or live-chat conversation with a due date/time and a short note. The reminder:

1. Persists per-user (`req.user!.id` scoped — never shared).
2. Fires an in-app `Notification` when it becomes due (background scheduler tick), so the agent sees it in the notification bell.
3. Appears in a personal to-do list on the dashboard, ordered by due date, with a "mark done" action.

**Not in scope:** email notification for due reminders (acceptance criteria doesn't require it — see intake notes); shared/team-visible reminders (personal only, per intake technical hints); quick replies (Story 23); internal-team collaboration (Story 24).

## Backend Tasks

### 1 — Create the `Reminder` Mongoose model

**Create file:** `backend/src/models/Reminder.ts`

Follow the `Message.ts` shape verbatim for the `parentType`/`parentId` pair:

```ts
import mongoose, { Document, Schema, Types } from "mongoose";

export type ReminderParentType = "ticket" | "conversation";

export interface IReminder extends Document {
  agent: Types.ObjectId;              // the owner — always req.user!.id
  parentType: ReminderParentType;     // "ticket" | "conversation"
  parentId: Types.ObjectId;           // Ticket._id or Conversation._id
  dueAt: Date;
  note: string;
  completed: boolean;                 // marked done by the agent
  notifiedAt: Date | null;            // set by the scheduler when the "reminder_due" notification fires — prevents double-firing
  createdAt: Date;
  updatedAt: Date;
}

const reminderSchema = new Schema<IReminder>(
  {
    agent: { type: Schema.Types.ObjectId, ref: "User", required: true, index: true },
    parentType: { type: String, enum: ["ticket", "conversation"], required: true },
    parentId: { type: Schema.Types.ObjectId, required: true },
    dueAt: { type: Date, required: true },
    note: { type: String, required: true, trim: true, maxlength: 500 },
    completed: { type: Boolean, default: false },
    notifiedAt: { type: Date, default: null },
  },
  { timestamps: true }
);

// Backs the "to-do list" query (mine, open, soonest first).
reminderSchema.index({ agent: 1, completed: 1, dueAt: 1 });
// Backs the scheduler sweep (due, not completed, not yet notified).
reminderSchema.index({ completed: 1, notifiedAt: 1, dueAt: 1 });

export const Reminder = mongoose.model<IReminder>("Reminder", reminderSchema);
```

**Do not** add a virtual populate — parent lookup is done in the router with two lean queries so a `ticket` reminder never accidentally leaks a `conversation` populate misconfig.

### 3 — Reminder-notification service helper

**File:** `backend/src/services/notification.service.ts`

Add a new export after `createTicketNotification` (currently ending line 19), mirroring its try/catch-and-log shape:

```ts
export async function createReminderDueNotification(params: {
  recipient: Types.ObjectId | string;
  reminderId: Types.ObjectId | string;
  parentType: "ticket" | "conversation";
  parentId: Types.ObjectId | string;
}): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await Notification.create({
      recipient: params.recipient,
      type: "reminder_due",
      reminderId: params.reminderId,
      ticketId: params.parentType === "ticket" ? params.parentId : null,
      conversationId: params.parentType === "conversation" ? params.parentId : null,
    });
  } catch (err) {
    console.error("[notifications] failed to create reminder_due", err);
  }
}
```

### 4 — Validation schemas

**Create file:** `backend/src/validation/reminder.schema.ts`

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { flexibleDateSchema } from "./common";

export const createReminderBodySchema = z.object({
  parentType: z.enum(["ticket", "conversation"], { error: "parentType must be ticket or conversation" }),
  parentId: z.string().regex(/^[0-9a-fA-F]{24}$/, "parentId must be a valid id"),
  dueAt: flexibleDateSchema(),
  note: z.string().trim().min(1, "note is required").max(500, "note must be ≤ 500 characters"),
});

export const updateReminderBodySchema = z.object({
  dueAt: flexibleDateSchema().optional(),
  note: z.string().trim().min(1).max(500).optional(),
  completed: z.boolean().optional(),
}).refine((v) => v.dueAt !== undefined || v.note !== undefined || v.completed !== undefined, {
  message: "at least one of dueAt, note, completed is required",
});

export const listRemindersQuerySchema = z.object({
  status: z.enum(["open", "completed", "all"]).optional().default("open"),
  page: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).optional().default(1),
  limit: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).max(50).optional().default(20),
});
```

Reuse `flexibleDateSchema` from `backend/src/validation/common.ts` (already imported by `me.schema.ts` line 3).

### 5 — REST endpoints (mount under `/api/v1/me/reminders`)

**File:** `backend/src/routes/me.routes.ts`

Add these routes **after** the existing `PATCH /notifications/:id/read` and **before** `GET /contact` (grep for both — their exact line numbers have drifted from any earlier citation, but the insertion point between them is unchanged). All handlers use `requireAuth`, role-guard `agent`/`admin`/`subadmin` (customers can't have reminders — return 403), scope every query on `agent: req.user!.id`, and confirm the referenced ticket/conversation exists before persisting.

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/me/reminders` | Create. Body: `createReminderBodySchema`. **Must** verify `parentId` exists in the matching collection (`Ticket` or `Conversation`) — 404 otherwise. Reject `dueAt` in the past (`< now - 60s`) with 400. |
| `GET` | `/me/reminders` | List **mine**. Query: `listRemindersQuerySchema`. Sort: `dueAt: 1` for `open`, `updatedAt: -1` for others. Populate `parentId` conditionally — split into two queries, one for `parentType === "ticket"` populating `ticketNumber subject`, one for `"conversation"` populating a display label (customer name / topic per the Conversation model). Return `{ reminders, total, page, limit }`. |
| `PATCH` | `/me/reminders/:id` | Update `dueAt` / `note` / `completed`. Body: `updateReminderBodySchema`. `findOneAndUpdate({ _id, agent: req.user!.id }, …)` — 404 if not found or not mine (never distinguish, per the mark-read precedent at lines 168–170). |
| `DELETE` | `/me/reminders/:id` | Delete. Same `{ _id, agent }` filter, same 404 shape. |

Every handler ends with `res.status(200).json({...})` (or 201 for POST). Do not throw — `errorHandler` catches everything.

**Role guard helper**: add at the top of the reminder block (or as a tiny local function) — reject `req.user!.role === "customer"` with `403 { error: "Only staff can set reminders" }`.

### 6 — Due-reminder scheduler

**Create file:** `backend/src/services/reminderScheduler.service.ts`

Poll every 60 seconds. On each tick:

```ts
const now = new Date();
const due = await Reminder.find({
  completed: false,
  notifiedAt: null,
  dueAt: { $lte: now },
}).limit(200).lean();

for (const r of due) {
  await createReminderDueNotification({
    recipient: r.agent,
    reminderId: r._id,
    parentType: r.parentType,
    parentId: r.parentId,
  });
  // Optional Socket.io push if the agent is online — see §7.
  await Reminder.updateOne({ _id: r._id, notifiedAt: null }, { $set: { notifiedAt: now } });
}
```

Export `startReminderScheduler(io: Server): () => void` (returns a stop-fn used by tests). Wrap the tick in try/catch and log — never let a failed sweep kill the interval. Guard with an `if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== "test")` in the start-fn so vitest doesn't inherit a background loop.

**File:** `backend/src/server.ts` — after `registerChatHandlers(io)` (line 19), add `startReminderScheduler(io);`.

If Story 27 (SLA scheduler) has already introduced a `services/scheduler.service.ts` with a "register tick" registry pattern, **register the reminder sweep as a tick there instead** of running a separate `setInterval`. Grep for `setInterval` under `backend/src/services/` before writing the file.

### 7 — Real-time Socket.io push (nice-to-have, best-effort)

**File:** `backend/src/sockets/chat.socket.ts` — grep for how the agent's userId is joined into a socket room (`socket.join(userId)` pattern). Emit `"reminder:due"` with `{ reminderId, parentType, parentId, note, dueAt }` to `io.to(String(r.agent)).emit(...)` from the scheduler in §6.

Frontend `NotificationBell.tsx` listens for `"reminder:due"` and prepends the item without waiting for the next poll. If the socket join key is not `userId` (grep will tell you), skip this section — the in-app `Notification` row from §3 is the authoritative delivery mechanism; realtime is icing.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **`dueAt` in the past on create** → 400 with `"dueAt must be in the future"`. Enforced in the router before persisting (§5). A 60-second grace (`< now - 60s`) tolerates client-clock skew.
- **Reminder points at a ticket that was later hard-deleted** → the list endpoint's `.populate("parentId", …)` returns null; router filters those rows out of the response (same guard as `me.routes.ts` line 123). Underlying doc is left in the DB for audit; a follow-up cleanup job can hard-delete orphaned reminders.
- **Reminder points at a closed conversation** → still valid; still surfaces on the dashboard. Closing a chat does not auto-complete pending reminders.
- **Owner is deactivated (`isActive: false`) between create and due-tick** → scheduler still writes the notification (harmless — the deactivated user can't log in to see it). Do **not** hard-delete on deactivate; a reactivated agent should see their history intact.
- **Scheduler sweep overlaps a slow tick** → `notifiedAt: null` in both the query filter and the `updateOne` filter make the update idempotent — a second concurrent sweep touching the same row would find `notifiedAt` already set and no-op. Enforced in `reminderScheduler.service.ts` §6.
- **Server restart between "create notification" and "set notifiedAt"** → next sweep re-fires the notification (best-effort delivery; duplicate in-app rows are less bad than a missed reminder). Documented in a comment in the scheduler file.
- **User creates 1000 reminders** → list endpoint caps `limit` at 50; scheduler caps its per-tick batch at 200. No unbounded reads.
- **Concurrent PATCH "mark done" while scheduler is mid-sweep** → race is benign: either the sweep sees `completed: false` and writes a notification (the agent completed it half a second later — acceptable), or it sees `completed: true` and skips.
- **Bilingual note** (Arabic/emoji/RTL characters in `note`) → stored as-is; frontend renders with the same `dir="auto"` shell used elsewhere.
- **`parentId` refers to a ticket the current user has no permission to view** → creation is still allowed (personal reminders are self-scoped); the ticket link in the to-do list will 403 on click, which is the caller's problem, not this feature's. Documented in the POST handler's comment.
- **Customer role tries to POST** → 403 (customers can't reach `/dashboard` anyway; belt-and-braces).

## Migration / Rollback

- **Schema.** No destructive migration. `Notification.ticketId` moves from `required` to `optional`; existing docs remain valid. `reminderId` and `conversationId` default to `null`; existing docs auto-populate `null` on read. `Reminder` is a brand-new collection — nothing to backfill.
- **Rollback.** Revert the three touched files (`Notification.ts`, `notification.service.ts`, `me.routes.ts`) and drop the `reminders` collection: `db.reminders.drop()`. The `reminder_due` rows in `notifications` should also be deleted: `db.notifications.deleteMany({ type: "reminder_due" })`. Any bell client rendering a `reminder_due` row after rollback would silently drop it (unknown type → default branch).
- **Half-applied state to watch for.** If the backend deploys before the frontend, the bell may receive a `reminder_due` payload with `ticketId: null` and hit the existing "drop rows without a ticket" filter — verify the `.filter((n) => n.ticketId || n.reminderId)` update from §2 lands **in the same deploy** as the model change.

6. **Notification bell:** with a reminder now overdue, refresh the header — bell shows a `reminder_due` item that links to the parent ticket/chat. `PATCH /me/notifications/:id/read` clears it.
7. **Bilingual:** toggle locale to Arabic; every reminder string is translated, RTL layout correct, "Mark done" button reads Arabic.
8. **Regression:** existing ticket-assignment notifications still fire (create a ticket, confirm the assignee's bell); nothing about ticket-anchored notifications changed visually.
